name: exec-summary-budget
prompt: This executive summary is going to the leadership team on Friday. Make it land without changing what it asks for.
expectations: The response applies at most three rhetorical figures and names each one with the trigger condition that licensed it

The response reports a claim check hedge by hedge, covering at least 'potentially', 'more difficult to quantify with precision', 'has not been fully assessed', 'financial modelling indicates', and 'should not be interpreted as a recommendation', and each hedge it reports as kept is actually present in the output
Every number in the source survives unchanged: four platforms, 2021 to 2024, $2.1M, eighteen months, three teams, month twenty-six, two of four platforms undocumented, two viable targets
The ask ('Leadership approval is requested to proceed with a detailed planning phase, with a decision gate...') is preserved in substance
The output adds no claim or commitment absent from the source, such as what the planning phase will resolve or who will own it
The output contains no negative parallelism and no generic positive closer ('the future is bright', 'poised for growth', 'we will lead')
The rewritten prose contains at most one anaphora run and no more than two em dashes in any paragraph (the change-note block is exempt)
